title: Gauss homogeneity and generic rank of the reduction of a finite Tate domain
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Write $V=\{a:|a|\le1\}$, $\mathfrak m=\{a:|a|<1\}$ and $k=V/\mathfrak m$. Let $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$, $d\ge0$, be a restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] with Gauss norm $\|\cdot\|_G$. Let $j:T\hookrightarrow C$ be an injective $K$-algebra homomorphism, where $C$ is a nonzero affinoid domain (a quotient of a restricted-series ring which has no zero divisors) finite as a $T$-module. Define $\rho_C(c)=\sup_{\mathfrak n\in\operatorname{Max}C}|c\bmod\mathfrak n|$, using the finite residue fields with their unique extending absolute values. Put $C^\circ=\{c:\rho_C(c)\le1\}$, $C^{\circ\circ}=\{c:\rho_C(c)<1\}$, $S=C^\circ/C^{\circ\circ}$, $R=k[U_1,\ldots,U_d]$, $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$. Then $\rho_C(j(t)c)=\|t\|_G\rho_C(c)$ for every $t\in T,c\in C$. Coefficient reduction identifies the reduction of $T$ with $R$, and $j$ induces an injective map $R\hookrightarrow S$. The ring $S$ is reduced and torsion-free as an $R$-module (a nonzero scalar in $R$ kills no nonzero element of $S$). For $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, the localization $S\otimes_R Q$ is a finite-dimensional $Q$-algebra and $\dim_Q(S\otimes_R Q)\le[E:F]$. No integrality or module-finiteness assertion about $S$ over $R$ is included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tate-fraction-orthogonal-spectral-norm] with $e=d$ and $L=E$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given completeness, nontrivial valuation, algebraic closedness, injective finite map and nonzero affinoid domain. It supplies $n=[E:F]<\infty$ and an $F$-vector-space norm $N$ restricting to $\rho_C$, with $N(fz)=|f|_FN(z)$ and $|t|_F=\|t\|_G$. Hence $\rho_C(j(t)c)=N(tc)=\|t\|_G\rho_C(c)$, including $t=0$ and $c=0$. Its explicit formula applied to the minimal polynomial $Z-1$ gives $\rho_C(1)=N(1)=1$, so $\rho_C(j(t))=\|t\|_G$. The orthogonal-basis assertion of that node is not needed.

proof.text: At each maximal ideal the residue absolute value is ultrametric and multiplicative; taking suprema gives $\rho_C(a+b)\le\max(\rho_C(a),\rho_C(b))$, $\rho_C(-a)=\rho_C(a)$ and $\rho_C(ab)\le\rho_C(a)\rho_C(b)$. The suprema are finite by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. Thus $C^\circ$ is a unital subring and $C^{\circ\circ}$ is an ideal of it: for the ideal product use $\rho_C(a)\le1$, $\rho_C(b)<1$. Consequently the displayed quotient $S$ is a ring. If a class represented by $c\in C^\circ$ has a positive power zero, then $\rho_C(c^h)<1$ for some $h\ge1$. The cited power formula yields $\rho_C(c)^h<1$, hence $\rho_C(c)<1$, and the class itself is zero. This proves reducedness.

source.place: Section 1.2, printed pp.8-9, and Section 1.4 Lemma 12, printed pp.25-27; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements, with the generic-rank argument supplied here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-tate-unit-ball-polynomial-reduction], coefficient reduction from $T^\circ=\{t:\|t\|_G\le1\}$ onto $R$ is surjective with kernel $T^{\circ\circ}=\{t:\|t\|_G<1\}$. This gives the asserted identification of the reduction of $T$. Step 1 shows that $j$ sends these two sets into $C^\circ$ and $C^{\circ\circ}$, respectively, and that $j(t)$ represents zero in $S$ exactly when $\|t\|_G<1$. Hence it induces an injective unital ring map $R\hookrightarrow S$, taking residue constants to residue constants. Also $R$ is a domain: nonzero $r,u\in R$ admit lifts $t,v$ of Gauss norm one, so $\|tv\|_G=1$ by [lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative]; their product has nonzero reduction.

source.place: Section 1.2, printed pp.8-9, and Section 1.4 Lemma 12, printed pp.25-27; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements, with the generic-rank argument supplied here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $0\ne r\in R$ and $0\ne s\in S$. Lift $r$ to $t\in T^\circ$ by step 3 and $s$ to $c\in C^\circ$ by the quotient definition. Nonvanishing of the reductions implies $\|t\|_G=1$ and $\rho_C(c)=1$. Step 1 gives $\rho_C(j(t)c)=1$, so its reduction $rs$ is nonzero. This proves the stated torsion-freeness, without identifying $S$ with a domain.

source.place: Section 1.2, printed pp.8-9, and Section 1.4 Lemma 12, printed pp.25-27; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements, with the generic-rank argument supplied here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $M=R\setminus\{0\}$. Since $R$ is a domain, $Q$ is its localization at $M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] to $R\to S$: it identifies the ring $W=S\otimes_RQ$ with the localization of $S$ at the image of $M$. Its $Q$-algebra structure has scalar map $q\mapsto1\otimes q$. Take a finite independent family $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ over $Q$ in $W$. The cited fraction representation gives $w_i=s_i\otimes(1/r_i)$ for $s_i\in S$ and $0\ne r_i\in R$. The vectors $s_i\otimes1=r_iw_i$ are independent: a relation with coefficients $q_i$ becomes $\sum_i(q_ir_i)w_i=0$, so every $q_i=0$. Choose lifts $c_i\in C^\circ$ of $s_i$.

source.place: Section 1.2, printed pp.8-9, and Section 1.4 Lemma 12, printed pp.25-27; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements, with the generic-rank argument supplied here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: These $c_i$ are independent over $F$. Indeed, a nonzero relation $\sum_i f_ic_i=0$ in $E$, $f_i\in F$, gives one $\sum_i t_ic_i=0$ with $t_i\in T$ not all zero after multiplying by the product of the nonzero denominators of the $f_i$. Since $C\hookrightarrow E$ is injective, this is an equality in $C$. The largest coefficient absolute value among all the finitely many restricted series $t_i$ is attained: choose any nonzero coefficient $a$; in each series only finitely many coefficients have absolute value at least $|a|$, and the maximum over their finite nonempty union dominates all remaining coefficients. Let $\lambda\in K^\times$ be a coefficient attaining that maximum and put $u_i=\lambda^{-1}t_i$. All $u_i$ have Gauss norm at most one and some has norm one. Reduce $\sum_i j(u_i)c_i=0$ in $S$: it gives $\sum_i\operatorname{red}(u_i)s_i=0$, with some $\operatorname{red}(u_i)\ne0$ by the kernel assertion of [lem-trf-tate-unit-ball-polynomial-reduction]. Tensoring gives a nonzero $Q$-linear relation on the independent $s_i\otimes1$ of step 5; nonzero coefficients remain nonzero in $Q$ because $R$ is a domain. This contradiction proves the independence.

source.place: Section 1.2, printed pp.8-9, and Section 1.4 Lemma 12, printed pp.25-27; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements, with the generic-rank argument supplied here. Primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-independent-family-card-le-dimension] to $c_1,\ldots,c_m$ in the finite-dimensional $F$-space $E$ from step 1. It gives $m\le n$. Therefore every finite independent family in $W$ has size at most $n$. Starting with the empty family, whenever its span is not all of $W$, choose one vector outside that span. The enlarged family is independent: in a relation with a nonzero coefficient of the new vector, division by that coefficient would put it in the old span. This process must stop by the $n$th addition, since otherwise it constructs $n+1$ independent vectors. The resulting family is a finite basis of size at most $n$. By [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] this proves finite dimensionality and gives $\dim_Q W\le n=[E:F]$. Its $Q$-algebra structure was established in step 5.
